---
title: "Getting started"
jupyter: php
---

This page assumes the `php` kernel is installed and `juphyter doctor` reports
it as ready. [Installation](install.qmd) covers both. The examples were run in
a Quarto document, and they behave the same way in a JupyterLab notebook.

To follow along in JupyterLab, run `jupyter lab` from an environment that has
it, such as `~/.venvs/juphyter/bin/jupyter lab`, and choose the PHP kernel in
the launcher. To follow along in Quarto, create a file `first.qmd`:

````markdown
---
title: "A first PHP document"
jupyter: php
---

```{{php}}
echo "sum: ", array_sum(range(1, 10)), "\n";
```
````

Then run `quarto render first.qmd`, which writes `first.html`.

## A first cell

A cell holds PHP without an opening `<?php` tag. Whatever the cell prints with
`echo` appears first, and the value of its last expression appears after it.

```{php}
$primes = [2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13];

echo count($primes), " primes, summing to ", array_sum($primes), "\n";

array_sum($primes) / count($primes);
```

A cell whose last expression is a statement or a call that returns `null`
shows only what it printed.

## State between cells

Variables, objects, functions, and classes carry from one cell to the next.

```{php}
$primes[] = 17;

$primes;
```

Restarting the kernel starts a new PHP session with nothing defined. In
JupyterLab, use **Kernel > Restart Kernel**. Each `quarto render` starts a new
session.

## Imports

A `use` statement applies to its own cell and to every later cell. A notebook
can put its imports in its first cell and use short names afterward. This
example uses [phibble](https://phibble.phpstats.org), which the `php` kernel
finds when the document sits inside a Composer project that requires it, or
which the `phpstats` kernel from
[Installation](install.qmd#the-phpstats-packages) provides.

```{php}
use Phibble\DataFrame;
```

```{php}
$orders = DataFrame::fromRows([
    ['channel' => 'web', 'region' => 'north', 'total' => 120.50],
    ['channel' => 'store', 'region' => 'north', 'total' => 80.00],
    ['channel' => 'web', 'region' => 'south', 'total' => 42.25],
]);

$orders;
```

A cell cannot declare a `namespace`, and it cannot declare a class or a
function that an earlier cell already declared. [Limitations](limitations.qmd)
explains both.

## Errors

A cell that throws shows the exception, its message, and a traceback whose
lines name the cell and the line number.

```{php}
#| error: true
$mean = fn (array $values) => array_sum($values) / count($values);

$mean([]);
```

The session survives the exception. Variables defined before it keep their
values.

Warnings, notices, and deprecations appear in the cell's error output, and the
cell keeps running.

```{php}
$widths = ['narrow' => 4, 'wide' => 12];

$widths['narrow'] + $widths['medium'];
```

## Rich output

The kernel sends each value in every format it can produce, and the front end
picks the one it can draw. A phibble data frame comes as an HTML table and as
the text phibble prints at a terminal. A phiz plot comes as a Vega-Lite
specification, as HTML, as a static SVG when vl-convert is installed, and as a
one-line text description.

Any class can provide its own output. A `toHtml(): string` method supplies
HTML, and a `toMimeBundle(): array` method supplies every format at once.

```{php}
final class Progress
{
    public function __construct(private readonly int $done, private readonly int $total) {}

    public function toHtml(): string
    {
        return sprintf(
            '<progress value="%d" max="%d"></progress> %d of %d',
            $this->done,
            $this->total,
            $this->done,
            $this->total,
        );
    }

    public function __toString(): string
    {
        return sprintf('%d of %d', $this->done, $this->total);
    }
}

new Progress(7, 9);
```

`Juphyter\display()` shows a value part way through a cell, so one cell can
show several tables or plots.

```{php}
Juphyter\display(new Progress(3, 9));
Juphyter\display(new Progress(9, 9));
```
